chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The scabbard of the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and its handle were of silver, and between that was a ring of silver. And I wore the armor of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and it dragged, and therein were three silver rings in front of it and two at the back of it.

key_terms.نَعْلُ: Scabbard or sheath of a sword

ai.seo_question: What were the materials and features of the Prophet Muhammad's sword and armor according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the modest yet dignified adornment of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny), specifically noting the silver details on his sword and the heavy, silver-ringed armor he wore. It serves as a practical example of the Ahl al-Bayt's simple lifestyle and their use of precious metals not for extravagance, but as part of their functional military gear, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the tangible heritage of the Prophet. The description of the armor's weight and the specific arrangement of the silver rings provides historical insight into the material culture of early Islamic leadership.
